points.t: An older person, often with dementia or Parkinson’s, with itchy ‘eczema’ or hives that will not settle, then tense blisters on the limbs and trunk.
Autoantibodies to BP180/BP230 at the basement membrane cause a subepidermal split; gliptins and loop diuretics are drug triggers.
Refer for biopsy; review gliptins; doxycycline 200 mg daily ± superpotent topical steroid (BLISTER trial); steroid safety if prednisolone is used.
Ocular mucous membrane pemphigoid (blindness), pemphigoid gestationis, and steroid toxicity in frail patients.

points: IgG (± IgE) autoantibodies to **BP180 (collagen XVII; NC16A domain)** and **BP230** in the hemidesmosome trigger complement activation, then eosinophil/neutrophil recruitment, proteases, and a **subepidermal** split in the lamina lucida.
**Quiz relevance:** the 85-year-old with **poorly controlled T2DM** is the classic patient on a gliptin. **Check the repeat list.**

**Prodrome (non-bullous phase):** weeks to months of **itch** with eczematous or **urticarial plaques** or excoriations alone. This is often misdiagnosed as "asteatotic eczema" or "scabies" in a care home.
**Mucosal involvement in only ~10–20%**, and it is mild. Prominent mucosal disease should make you think of **MMP**.
Nikolsky sign is usually negative. Eosinophilia is common.
ELISA anti-BP180 (which roughly follows activity) and anti-BP230; indirect IMF on salt-split skin (epidermal side).
Before treatment: glucose/HbA1c, BP, bone health, renal function (doxycycline is fine in CKD; check other drugs), and a baseline weight.

items.t: Eye redness, grittiness or scarring with oral erosions: **mucous membrane pemphigoid**, same-week ophthalmology (same day if vision affected).
Hoarseness or stridor: airway involvement, emergency.
Blistering rash in **pregnancy** starting round the umbilicus: urgent dermatology and obstetrics.
Extensive blistering or secondary infection in a frail patient: same-day assessment.

pearls.t: **"Itchy elderly patient with eczema that won't settle" may be BP before the blisters appear.** Refer for biopsy with DIF when the itch is out of proportion and standard treatment fails.
In care homes, **exclude scabies** (burrows, other residents itching) in parallel, since the two can coexist.
Patient support: PEMFriends; BAD leaflet *Bullous pemphigoid*.
